resolution: Built per-face model painting on the viewer — fill a face, paint any face — the durable replacement for the Studio's broken paint. Root cause we'd diagnosed (req_2115): uvDedup.ts fuses every congruent face onto ONE shared UV-atlas island, so painting one panel repaints its identical twins, and degenerate unwrap islands leave faces unpaintable. This design makes that impossible: the resident mesh is non-indexed (each face owns its 3 verts), so each face gets its OWN texel in a small host-owned WxH paint atlas and its verts map to that texel — per-face color rides the EXISTING scene3d diffuse-texture path with ZERO shader change. New framework/gpu/model_paint.zig holds the active-target state + Moller-Trumbore raycast + atlas build (headless unit tests, test-model-paint). 3d.zig captures the exact render camera each frame and binds the target's paint atlas as its diffuse; the load door calls setPaintTarget (rewriting UVs in place before upload). Doors: __model_paint_at(x,y,r,g,b) raycasts the cursor and fills the hit face (click=one face, drag=stroke), plus __model_paint_face/__model_face_count for index fills. cart/modelview gains Paint mode (P key), a 10-swatch palette, and a white material so paint shows true. Proof: RJIT_PAINT rainbows every face by index and all 180 car faces render their OWN color — the congruent-panel fusion that plagued the Studio is structurally gone; unpainted load stays clean grey; the raycast math is unit-tested and feeds the captured render camera so click-to-paint lands live.
